newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads steadfast vs issuance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads steadfast vs issuance.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads weathered the second consecutive $1.0 billion-plus day of high-grade issuance on Wednesday, with only spots of widening seen, dealers said.

Talk of market softness due to new issue volume was widespread but evidence was hard to find. New issues were trading in line with original prices with the possible exception of the most aggressive deals, traders said.
"It's a little softer but holding in, definitely better than people seem to be talking about," one high-grades trader said. "Things may feel heavy but nothing's specifically wider."

Topping investment grade issuance, Ford Motor Co issued $500 million 50-year A1/A-plus rated debentures as 7.40s to yield 7.477 percent or 77 basis points over the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond. Goldman, Sachs & Co is lead manager on the deal.
Traders said the Ford debt, which typically comes rich to the market, will likely see some widening when freed.

Earlier, May Department Stores set $125 million A2/single-A rated 10-year notes via Morgan Stanley at par to yield 6.875 percent for a 51 basis point spread. The notes were freed and quoted with a 53 bid, 51 market near the close, one trader said.
In other high-grade issuance:

-Praxair Inc tapped the market with $250 million in A3/BBB-plus rated 10-year notes, priced at par to yield 6.90 percent or 52 basis points over the Treasury curve. The deal was managed by a Morgan Stanley & Co syndicate.
-Heller Financial Inc issued $200 million A2/BBB-plus five-year senior notes via J.P. Morgan Securities, priced as 6-1/2s to yield 6.578 percent for a 49 basis point spread.
Traders also said secondary prices and tone suffered not to fundamentals but because of the unilateral focus on new issues on Wednesday and the promise of much more this week.
In one offering, Banque Nationale de Paris plans to sell $350 million in A1/A-rated 12-year debt via Salomon Brothers at a spread of 80 to 82 basis points, sources said.

The broad corporate market tracked U.S. Treasuries first higher then lower as the Street dissected some potent economic data, traders said. Governments, initially higher on bullish sentiments and a benign read of third quarter GDP, broke lower soon after a report that home sales remained at lofty levels and the Beige Book report denoted moderate growth and tight labor markets, analysts said.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
Turning to high-yielders, traders said prices saw no widespread deterioration amid new supply there. In fact, some large issues traded higher in the aftermarket.

International Home Foods Inc's $400 million 144a 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced on Tuesday at par to yield 10.375 percent via a Chase Securities Inc syndicate, were quoted at 101 at the close.
Australis Media's $150 million 144a issue of Tuesday was less successful, traders said, and lead manager Salomon Brothers was forced to buy part of the deal.
Taiwan's Total Access Communication stirred markets on Wednesday with a $400 million two part rule 144a Ba1/BBB-minus rated non-callable issue via lead manager UBS Securities Inc.

The first tranche of $100 million five-year notes was priced as 7-5/8s to yield 7.632 percent or 150 basis points over Treasuries. Another $300 million 10-year notes were priced as 8-3/8s to yield 8.409 percent or 200 basis points over Treasuries.
In spot news, Ralph's Grocery Co's 11s fell one point to 99-3/4 bid, par offer after news of a proposed $3.25 billion Safeway Inc/Vons Cos merger heightened competition concerns.
